items.title: Show HN: Aakit – find every assumption your coding agent made, and which broke
items.why_it_matters: Aakit is a new tool designed to trace and surface every assumption a coding agent makes while writing code, highlighting which ones actually broke during execution. As someone vibe coding where the AI types and you direct, your biggest bottleneck is verifying the AI's work; this tool gives you a clear audit log of what Claude assumed about your codebase. Try running the tool on your AI-ingest repository this week to see exactly where Claude's logic diverged from your actual Supabase schema or Next.js setup.

items.title: Show HN: Brave DevTools MCP – Control Brave from Claude, Codex, and Cursor
items.why_it_matters: The Brave DevTools MCP server lets Claude, Codex, or Cursor directly inspect and control your Brave browser's developer tools. Instead of copy-pasting console errors or network failures from your Next.js frontend back into Claude, the agent can read the DevTools console and inspect the DOM directly to debug itself. Try installing this MCP server today and ask Claude Code to debug a rendering error on your local Next.js dev server.

items.title: Show HN: Cc-probeline – Claude Code status line with Fable limits and turn costs
items.why_it_matters: Cc-probeline is a lightweight status line utility for Claude Code that displays your current Fable limits and real-time turn costs directly in your terminal. Since you are using Claude Code heavily to build AI-ingest, keeping an eye on token spend prevents surprise bills and helps you optimize how many turns you give the agent. Try cloning the repo and adding it to your terminal profile this week to track your exact spend during your next coding session.

items.title: Show HN: Claude Code kept ignoring our MCP tools, so we used hooks instead
items.why_it_matters: The creators of Graft released a workaround for when Claude Code ignores custom MCP tools, using terminal-based hooks instead to force reliable tool execution. If you are trying to hook up custom APIs or local scripts to help build AI-ingest and finding that Claude Code silently bypasses your MCP configuration, this hook-based pattern ensures your commands actually run. Try reviewing their simple hook implementation in the repository and apply it to your project this week if Claude starts ignoring your custom scripts.

items.title: `whoport` – which agent is using localhost:3000?
items.why_it_matters: Whoport is a tiny utility that identifies exactly which agent or background process is currently holding onto a local port like localhost:3000. When vibe coding with multiple terminal windows or background agents, Next.js will frequently crash on startup because a previous agent process didn't close cleanly and locked the port. Try running the tool the next time your Next.js dev server blocks you, so you can instantly kill the rogue agent process and keep shipping.

items.title: Rootless Container Sandbox for Claude Code and Codex
items.why_it_matters: This lightweight, rootless container sandbox is built specifically to run Claude Code and Codex safely on your local machine without giving the agent full access to your system. Because Claude Code executes terminal commands directly, running it inside this sandbox protects your personal files and system configuration from accidental destructive commands. Try setting up this sandbox on your laptop this week before your next major coding session to let Claude run and test code with zero risk to your machine.
